fact_checks.claim: The body states that k = 2 had the highest silhouette score and that inertia stopped falling around k = 3.
fact_checks.evidence: Page 10 Figure 6 reports silhouette 0.41 / 0.42 / 0.43 for k = 2 / 3 / 4, so the maximum is k = 4, and inertia falls by 59 for both k = 2->3 and k = 3->4, so the break is not at k = 3.

fact_checks.claim: Table 5 reports treated coefficient -0.211 with SE 0.126, t -3.204, p 0.003, and 95% CI -0.658 to -0.146.
fact_checks.evidence: Coefficient -0.211 with SE 0.126 implies t = -1.67; the printed CI midpoint is -0.402, which matches t = -3.19. The coefficient column is inconsistent with the t and CI columns.

fact_checks.claim: The body states the treated x time interaction has p = 0.047.
fact_checks.evidence: Table 5 on the same page reports p = 0.01 for treated * time.

fact_checks.claim: Table 2's After Diff (T - C) row has standard error, t, and p values supporting the text's 'p > 0.05'.
fact_checks.evidence: The three cells print 'null', so the text's assertion cannot be traced to any computation.

fact_checks.claim: Figure 11 shows that the six MIC values remain stable near the gray dotted line after noise injection.
fact_checks.evidence: Figure 11 is a decorative Wi-Fi icon with no plotted data, axis, or reference line.

fact_checks.claim: The DID effect for Critical Information Infrastructure Protection was 0.286, showing no significant impact, yet the post-period difference of 0.634 shows the treatment group had higher cybercrime.
fact_checks.evidence: A non-significant net effect cannot coexist with a causal claim drawn from the post-period raw difference; no standard error, p-value, or confidence interval is reported for either number.

fact_checks.claim: A high CEI score indicates significant exposure.
fact_checks.evidence: Page 7 applies (1 - CEI) x 100 and states that higher values then mean lower exposure, so the same acronym denotes two opposite directions across adjacent pages.

Both the contents page and the body go from '7 Sensitivity Analysis' to '9 Model Evaluation and Further Discussion'; no Section 8 exists. Separately, the numbered items '1.' to '4.' under 4.3.1 and the six policy themes under 5.2 are typeset at heading size, so they read as section headings although they are list items.

fact_checks.claim: The reference list supports the paper's data sources and methods.
fact_checks.evidence: Six of the ten entries are never cited in the body, including the NCSI, VERIS, CEI, ITU GCI, and MIC methodology sources.

fact_checks.claim: The paper concludes with model evaluation and recommendations.
fact_checks.evidence: The last content is ChatGPT advice on beautifying line charts; there is no conclusion or recommendation section.

g7_warnings.warning: A decorative icon is presented as a quantitative result figure. Any reader or judge who inspects it will treat the entire MIC robustness claim as unsupported.
The treated row cannot be reproduced from its own t and CI columns. Either the coefficient or the t/p/CI block must be recomputed before any downstream use.
Literal 'null' strings in SE, t, and p cells are an unresolved placeholder, not a rounding artifact.
Eight pages of pasted chat transcript exceed what a use-of-AI disclosure should contain and displace the conclusion section.
The clustering narrative and Figure 6 disagree on which k maximises the silhouette score; the chosen k = 3 is therefore unjustified as written.
No parallel-trends test, placebo test, or event-study plot is reported for any of the six DID themes, and treatment groups contain only one or two countries.
134 occurrences of ' - ' inside compound words, including in section titles, the contents page, and reference URLs.
Figure captions 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and Table 6 omit the space between number and title, while Tables 1-5 include it.
Promotional QR code ('MATHmodels / 关注数学模型 / 获取更多资讯') in the lower right corner; also a diagonal pink watermark over the text layer.
Statistical tables omit sample size, R-squared on three of four DID tables, F statistic, and any statement of the standard-error type.
No equation is numbered anywhere, although nine cross-referenced quantities (beta, composite score, NSCI regression) are defined in them.
No 'Section X' internal cross-reference appears, so method details cannot be located from the results chapters.
The framework flow chart has neither a number nor a caption, leaving a gap in the figure sequence.
Cluster outcomes are stated causally ('strengths result in lower rates of successful cyberattacks') although only cross-sectional clustering was performed.
MIC values are compared across variables as if they ranked causal importance, although MIC is symmetric and direction-free.
Section 9.3 ends about 55 percent down the page and the remainder is blank.
